questions.question: In the context of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes, what is the major organic product when CH₃CH₂CH₃ + 5 O₂ reacts under the following conditions: Spark / Thermal ignition (Δ)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Exothermic combustion of an alkane in excess oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water vapor. The correct major product is '3 CO₂(g) + 4 H₂O(g)'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes, what is the major organic product when C₁₀H₂₂ reacts under the following conditions: Zeolite catalyst, 500°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: High-temperature catalytic cracking cleaves long alkane carbon-carbon bonds into smaller alkanes and alkenes. The correct major product is 'C₅H₁₂ (Pentane) + C₅H₁₀ (Pentene)'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes, what is the major organic product when Cyclohexane reacts under the following conditions: Pt/Al₂O₃ catalyst, 300°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Catalytic reforming aromatizes cyclohexane to benzene driven by the large aromatic stabilization energy. The correct major product is 'Benzene (C₆H₆) + 3 H₂'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes, what is the major organic product when CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (n-Butane) reacts under the following conditions: AlCl₃ / HCl, 100°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Lewis acid-promoted carbocation rearrangement converts straight-chain butane to its branched isomer. The correct major product is '(CH₃)₂CHCH₃ (Isobutane / 2-Methylpropane)'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes, what is the major organic product when CH₄ + Cl₂ reacts under the following conditions: hν irradiation or 250°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Photochemical radical chain substitution yielding chloromethane and hydrogen chloride byproduct. The correct major product is 'CH₃Cl (Chloromethane) + HCl'.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Cyclopropane into CH₃CH₂CH₃ (Propane) in Alkanes and Cycloalkanes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Cyclopropane' → 'CH₃CH₂CH₃ (Propane)' specifically requires 'H₂ / Pd-C, 25°C'. Mechanistic basis: Severe angle strain (~115 kJ/mol) promotes catalytic ring opening of cyclopropane by hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Cyclopropane into Br-CH₂-CH₂-CH₂-Br (1,3-Dibromopropane) in Alkanes and Cycloalkanes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Cyclopropane' → 'Br-CH₂-CH₂-CH₂-Br (1,3-Dibromopropane)' specifically requires 'Br₂ / FeBr₃ catalyst, 25°C'. Mechanistic basis: Electrophilic cleavage driven by relief of ring strain yields an open-chain 1,3-dihaloalkane.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert cis-1-tert-Butyl-4-methylcyclohexane into Conformer with equatorial tert-butyl group (>99.9%) in Alkanes and Cycloalkanes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'cis-1-tert-Butyl-4-methylcyclohexane' → 'Conformer with equatorial tert-butyl group (>99.9%)' specifically requires 'Conformational equilibrium (25°C)'. Mechanistic basis: Extreme 1,3-diaxial steric clash (A-value ~ 20 kJ/mol) locks the bulky tert-butyl group in the equatorial position.

questions.question: Which starting material yields '(CH₃)₃C-Br (tert-Butyl bromide) + HBr' when treated with 'hν, 25°C photolysis' according to the principles of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes?
questions.explanation: Starting material deduction: Treating '(CH₃)₃CH + Br₂' with 'hν, 25°C photolysis' yields '(CH₃)₃C-Br (tert-Butyl bromide) + HBr'. Mechanistic rationale: Bromine radical selectively abstracts the weakest tertiary C-H bond with >99% regioselectivity.

questions.question: Which starting material yields 'CH₂=CH₂ (Ethylene) + H₂' when treated with 'Steam cracking at 800°C' according to the principles of Alkanes and Cycloalkanes?
questions.explanation: Starting material deduction: Treating 'CH₃-CH₃' with 'Steam cracking at 800°C' yields 'CH₂=CH₂ (Ethylene) + H₂'. Mechanistic rationale: Thermal industrial dehydrogenation of ethane to ethylene.
